Held notes swell in slowly. The main envelope adds Fold (+0.968) and opens the cutoff (+0.328) as each note opens. Key pressure adds Saturate (+0.170), Fold (+0.486) and cutoff (+0.187) and lowers Noise through Assign 2 (−0.125); the synced sawtooth LFO adds Noise through Assign 1 (+0.203).
The PRESSURE matrix row follows the instrument's global expression setting, which the export does not record.
Turning Shape up raises Noise and makes the pad work as a noisy bass in the low register, as heard from 05:15 in GitP/A/Session/26/11/01-Sun.

In that session the Launchpad Pro played it from 00:00 to 18:17. Recorded knob changes covered the main and cycling envelopes, filter amount, Spice, LFO rate and the three oscillator controls, with brief cutoff and resonance changes. A read of slot 259 after the session matched the October 25 export, so the slot still holds the factory sound. The session MIDI holds those knob changes as controller messages.

A short lead two octaves up: the main envelope has no attack and no sustain, and it opens the cutoff (+0.444) on each note. Key pressure is the main expressive control, driving Fold at full amount (+1.000) and Saturate (+0.373). The square LFO adds a small pitch modulation (+0.073) whose speed follows the LFO rate.
The PRESSURE matrix row follows the instrument's global expression setting, which the export does not record.

The Assign 3 destination is unresolved. Its saved destination ID is 0x0904, which the Freakout live map lists as an address of the Assign 3 field itself. Assign 3 stores the same ID in 70 of the 384 Factory 6.0 presets. In the session commentary at 21:28, the instrument shows this KEY/ARP → Assign 3 destination as "move".

In GitP/A/Session/26/11/01-Sun it was played from the MicroFreak keys from 18:17 to the end, with almost continuous pressure and pitch bends from 22:46. Recorded knob changes covered attack, decay, sustain, the cycling envelope, filter amount, the free LFO rate, Noise and Fold. At 25:15 pressure was routed through Assign 1 to the main envelope's attack, a matrix edit the capture does not record. A read of slot 260 after the session matched the October 25 export, so the slot still holds the factory sound. The session MIDI holds the knob changes as controller messages.

An archived GitP.24.11.23.C.mfpz patch contains this preset name. It shares its stored digital oscillator Type and two oscillator parameter fields with the archived Microfreak/Preset/368 TMF.24.11.23.B and Microfreak/Preset/370 TMF.24.11.23.D patches. Compared with B, the remaining oscillator field, filter cutoff, and resonance differ. Compared with D, a different oscillator field and the filter cutoff differ, while resonance matches. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/02 Param Controls describes Type and its three shaping controls.

The MicroFreak user guide documents the instrument and its controls.
Congratulations on your purchase of the Arturia MicroFreak!
The MicroFreak is a compact, versatile, semi-modular synthesizer with many distinctive features. It lets you experiment with modular sound construction without patch cords.

The standard MicroFreak and MicroFreak Vocoder Edition share the instrument's core features. The Vocoder Edition has a white casing and a gooseneck microphone; see Microfreak/UG/19 Appendix B Vocoder for its specific features.

Its digital oscillator and analog filter combine a broad range of digital sounds with a warm analog character. A cycling envelope adds modulation options associated with high-end modular systems, and the modulation matrix routes sources to many destinations.
The pressure-sensitive touch keyboard, paraphonic playing, arpeggiator, and assignable modulation destinations make the MicroFreak suited to expressive performance.
The MicroFreak is a USB MIDI Class Compliant device and can connect to compatible devices without installing drivers. Connecting an iPad may require a camera connection or USB-to-Lightning cable.
Two paraphonic sequencers can record and play up to four voices at once, sharing one filter; each sequencer has four modulation tracks.
